stage: a 32-file adversarial audit of my projections: what survived triage
why: the author asked for maximum parallelism, so I ran a read-only audit fleet over the thirty-two projection files I own: one audit agent per file, then a verifier agent for each high-severity candidate. Forty-four child agents in total ran against the checkout and modified nothing
the_result: NINE of the thirty-two files came back with candidate findings. The first candidate I triaged myself is REFUTED: PcChatContent L185-191 was reported as a crash risk and a false runtime claim, but ConditionPhrases.Kind takes a STRING (line 107), and every op reaching it is extracted by Ops() at line 637, which adds an op ONLY when it is a JsonValue string and otherwise records a malformed finding. So there is no crash there and no false claim
what_it_corroborated: independently flagged my own reported defect in ConditionPhrases L79 (the unguarded cast), and produced candidates in CutsceneActions, GameSettingsSurface, InvestigationPuzzle, KitTakeover, MaterialModes, ItemSpawns, Vehicles and StudioWritePaths
the_rule_i_am_holding: an audit candidate is not a finding until I have read the runtime consumer myself. Earlier tonight I reported a consequence from a single consumer and was wrong, and this same fleet's first candidate was wrong, which is exactly why each remaining candidate is being verified one by one against the code it depends on
